item.title: Lost Luggage, Redeemed Souls — Elder Gary E. Stevenson | EQ/RS Lesson Prep
item.description: A lesson-preparation walkthrough of Elder Gary E. Stevenson's April 2026 general conference talk "Lost Luggage, Redeemed Souls." The episode walks the talk end to end: the airport opening (33 million bags mishandled in 2024), Kansai International Airport in Osaka — 30 years and hundreds of millions of pieces without losing one single item — and the reason why, which is not technology but kaizen, "a quiet discipline of always looking for small ways to make processes better," plus the detail that improvements come from the people doing the everyday work. It then follows Elder Stevenson's turn from logistics to redemption: Heavenly Father sending His most precious belongings into mortality, parents and ministering brothers and sisters as stewards, the curb-and-platform farewell, and the claim written on the heart — "You are mine. I know you. You are not alone. I have not forgotten you. I intend to bring you home." Covers both of his cases (ministering, with Moroni 6:4 and D&C 20:53 and his four invitations; and the rising generation, with D&C 93:40, President Uchtdorf's promise, and President Nelson on learning to hear the Spirit). Includes a full section on the one place this lesson can go wrong and how Elder Stevenson defuses it himself — "Unlike pieces of luggage, each of us is ultimately responsible for our decisions, beliefs, and actions" — plus teaching angles for an elders quorum, four discussion questions ranked by risk, three things to avoid, and a minute-by-minute 40-minute lesson plan. All quotes verbatim.

item.title: Come Home — Elder Clark G. Gilbert | EQ/RS Lesson Prep
item.description: A lesson-preparation walkthrough of Elder Clark G. Gilbert's April 2026 general conference talk "Come Home" (his first address as an Apostle). The episode frames the lesson around two of the Savior's names — Redeemer and Repairer — then walks through the doctrine of the open door (choices have consequences, but the Savior still allows us to change) and the four people Elder Gilbert ministers to: those who feel they don't belong (Sister Anglesey), those who feel they don't measure up (Brother Vargas — "you don't have to be perfect... do your best, and Christ will make up the difference"), those who doubt (the Valdez family — anchor in what you do believe and recognize the Holy Ghost), and those bound by tradition (John Raass). It closes with the two audiences — those helping someone home and those finding their own way home — the BYU "we saved a seat just for you" flashlight image, and a suggested 40-minute lesson outline with discussion questions and scripture cross-references. Verbatim key quotes from Elder Gilbert, President Nelson, and President Oaks throughout.
